trials.claim: Send the same prompt to up to four models to compare answers
trials.claimQuote: Select up to four models and send the same prompt to all of them, so you can compare answers and pick the best one before acting
trials.reasoning: A buyer review and the vendor page both say you can send the same prompt to four models at once and compare them side by side. The credit-cost exhibits do not deny that capability, only that using it costs credits.

exhibits.quote: A one-page answer uses about 1 to 5 credits on a lighter model, 5 to 20 on a medium model, and 15 to 35 on a higher-end model.
exhibits.argument: Comparing the same prompt across four models multiplies credit cost 4x, undermining the claim of freely comparing answers.

exhibits.quote: Just hight light to founder to find way to optimize credit usage which is my concern at the moment(credit run out fast even select not latest model)
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports credits deplete rapidly even on cheaper models, limiting practical use of multi-model comparison.

exhibits.quote: Model comparison: over 200 models in one place, with the option to send the same prompt to four models at once.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms the platform lets you send the same prompt to four models at once to compare answers.

exhibits.quote: Compare models side by side on the same prompt, search the web, or run deep research without leaving the thread.
exhibits.argument: Vendor page states you can compare models side by side on the same prompt in one thread.

trials.claim: Access 200+ AI models with org-wide memory and team collaboration in one workspace
trials.claimQuote: Speed up daily work with AI using 200+ models, org-wide memory, and team collaboration
trials.reasoning: The vendor confirms 200+ models including GPT, Claude and Gemini in one workspace, and organization memory grounding agents in company knowledge. The credit exhibits show use is metered, but do not contradict that these features exist.

exhibits.quote: When your workspace has used all its credits, it cannot be used until more are available.
exhibits.argument: Org-wide memory and collaboration stop entirely when pooled credits are exhausted, contradicting unlimited workspace access.

exhibits.quote: A credit is how WorkLLM measures the AI work you use. It reflects the model provider's cost plus storage, infrastructure, and platform costs.
exhibits.argument: Access to 200+ models is metered by credits that include provider plus platform fees, not included unlimited access.

exhibits.quote: Access GPT, Claude, Gemini, and 200+ other models in one workspace. No vendor lock-in, and every new model update is available instantly.
exhibits.argument: Vendor confirms 200+ models including GPT, Claude, Gemini are available in one workspace.

exhibits.quote: Organization memory, grounds every AI agent automatically in your company's own knowledge
exhibits.argument: Vendor pricing page confirms org-wide memory that grounds agents in company knowledge.

trials.claim: Run GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral and 200+ others from single interface without separate subscriptions
trials.claimQuote: Run GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, and 200+ others from a single interface—no separate subscriptions requiredSelect up to four models and send the same prompt to all of them, so you can compare answers and pick the best one before actingFilter models by task type, cost, strength, or more to match the right model to what you're actually trying to do
trials.reasoning: The vendor confirms one chat with 200+ models and no vendor lock-in. The BYOK exhibit describes an optional bring-your-own-key category and the credit exhibit describes platform credits, neither showing separate model subscriptions are required.

exhibits.quote: BYOK Models you bring on your own, don’t use WorkLLM credits for the model itself.
exhibits.argument: Vendor admits some models require bringing your own API key, contradicting no separate subscriptions required.

exhibits.quote: When a workspace has used all its available credits, it can’t keep using the platform until more are available.
exhibits.argument: Single-interface access is gated by paid credits that must be repurchased, undermining no separate subscription claim.

exhibits.quote: One chat. 200+ models. Your whole team.
exhibits.argument: Vendor headline confirms single interface provides 200+ models for the whole team.

exhibits.quote: AI Chat (200+ AI models): Ask anything, compare answers across 200+ models, no vendor lock-in.
exhibits.argument: Vendor pricing confirms 200+ models accessible in one chat with no vendor lock-in, meaning no separate subscriptions.

trials.claim: Filter models by task type, cost and strength to match the task
trials.claimQuote: Filter models by task type, cost, strength, or more to match the right model to what you're actually trying to do
trials.reasoning: No exhibit shows whether models can be filtered by task type, cost or strength. The reviews only complain that credits burn quickly, which does not prove or disprove the filtering feature.

exhibits.quote: Burned about 200 credits in under an hour writing a series of 9 email outlines, a few blog outlines, and some misc. random chats.
exhibits.argument: High credit burn makes filtering by cost ineffective because even filtered tasks consume excessive credits quickly.

exhibits.quote: the credits burn way, way, way too quickly - even when using the "suggested" AI models.
exhibits.argument: Even using suggested filtered models still burns credits excessively, undermining cost-based filtering benefit.
